name: upx
why: Executable packer that transforms binaries is a fun way to watch compression rewrite programs, though it is widely known.

brief.what_it_is: UPX is a command-line executable packer that compresses programs and DLLs so they take up less disk space. You give it an executable file and it writes a compressed executable back out. The compressed file is self-contained and runs as before, with no separate runtime. The homepage says it supports Windows programs and DLLs, macOS apps and Linux executables, while the GitHub README names only Windows and Linux. It also has list, test and unpack modes, and keeps internal checksums of the compressed and uncompressed file.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a way to cut file size, typically by around 50%-70%, which saves disk space, network load and download time, and distribution and storage costs. The README frames it as a free, secure, portable, extendable, high-performance packer.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. The homepage says decompression happens in place, so compressed programs have no memory overhead, and that decompression runs at more than 500 MB/sec on a modern machine. It also says the format is documented and open, so security and antivirus tools can inspect UPX-compressed files.

commands_seen.context: Compresses a program or DLL with default settings.
Recommended by the README for better compression results.
Recommended by the README as an alternative for better compression; it is slower and tries harder.

brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the brew install was mentioned in the README or homepage. The homepage has a 'Download latest release' link. The README says the full documentation is in doc/upx-doc.txt, and that 'upx --help' prints usage.
brief.standout: The project is explicit that it will never add protection or encryption, because it considers such protectors a false sense of security. It is positioned as an open, inspectable packer that security tools can unpack and verify, which is unusual for a tool that rewrites binaries.
brief.status: maintained. The README copyright runs through 1996-2026, and it links to an active GitHub issue tracker. I did not find a last release date or last commit date in the pages I read.
brief.caveats: The README warns that UPX inherits the security context of any file it handles: packing, unpacking, testing or listing a file carries the same risk as running it, so use it only on trusted files. The homepage and README disagree on macOS support. The README says the UPX License Agreements apply, and the homepage says it is free for commercial use under GPLv2+ with exceptions. The brew caveats field was empty.
quotes: UPX is a free, secure, portable, extendable, high-performance executable packer for several executable formats.
We will *NOT* add any sort of protection and/or encryption. This only gives people a false feeling of security because all "protectors" can be broken by definition.
IMPORTANT NOTE: UPX inherits the security context of any files it handles.
